title: Sharing things out equally
examples: What if some are left over?

explain.say: Imagine you have twelve strawberries and three friends. How can you share them fairly, so everyone gets the same? Look at the board. Three plates, and the strawberries are shared out.
Share one at a time, like dealing cards. One for you, one for you, one for you. Everyone has one. Keep going until they are all gone! Can you pretend to deal them out?
Keep dealing: two each now. Six strawberries are on the plates, and six are still waiting. Can you guess how many each friend will get?
All twelve are shared out: four on each plate. Twelve shared between three is four. That is called dividing! Every plate has the same, so it is fair. Count each plate to check.
Try ten grapes shared between two. Five each! Great sharing. Your brain learns in its own way, and lots of brilliant people learn like this. Challenge: share some buttons between two teddies.

faq.a: It means giving everyone exactly the same amount, so it is fair. Twelve strawberries shared by three gives four each.

faq.q: How do I share things out?
faq.a: Deal them one at a time to each group, round and round, until there are none left. Then count one group.
Dividing means sharing into equal groups. Twelve divided by three is four.

faq.q: What if there are some left over?
faq.a: Sometimes things do not share equally. The ones left over are called the remainder. Seven sweets shared by two is three each, with one left over.

faq.q: How do I check my sharing?
faq.a: Count each group. If every group has the same, you shared it equally. Add the groups back together and you get the number you started with.
asks: How do I know it is fair?

facts: Things left over after sharing equally are called the remainder.

quiz.say: Share 10 grapes between 2 friends. How many does each get?
quiz.show: 10 grapes shared by 2: how many each?
quiz.why: Five and five make ten, so each friend gets five.

wrong.1: Eight is ten take away two. Sharing splits ten into two equal groups.
wrong.2: Twelve is ten add two. Sharing makes smaller groups.

quiz.say: What is the best way to share fairly?
quiz.show: The best way to share fairly?

options.show: Deal one at a time to each
options.say: Deal one at a time to each

options.show: Give them all to one person
options.say: Give them all to one person

quiz.why: Dealing one at a time makes sure everyone gets the same.

wrong.1: That is not fair: the others get none.
wrong.2: Handfuls can be different sizes, so it may not be fair.
